summary: Iteration 32 — Backend verification of Google Sheets column-mapping case-sensitivity fix. All 12/12 new tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_sheet_orders_case_fix.py and all 8/8 smart_search regression tests pass. T1 (data migration): admin's settings.sheet.column_mapping now has 'Tracking Id' and 'Master Order Id' (title-case, no uppercase 'ID' variants left). T2 (the reported bug): GET /api/sheets/orders on admin's 329-row sheet now returns total=329 shipped=311 not_shipped=18 (94.5% flagged already_shipped) — massive drop from the pre-fix state where all 329 were 'New Orders'. T3 (_row_key case-insensitive): identical row_key across 'Order ID' vs 'Order Id' vs 'order id' casing confirmed. T4 (canonical casing regression): fast-path still returns correct values. T5 (alias resolution): customer_phone ↔ phone still resolves after the case fix. T6 (smart_search regression): 8/8 pass, no collateral damage.  IMPORTANT FINDING: server.sheets_orders (server.py lines 1197-1485) is orphan code — it is NOT registered on any route. The live handler is routers/sheets.py lines 194-395 which was NOT updated with the case-insensitive mapped_field fallback. It only benefits from the _row_key fix (imported from server.py). Today's data works because Fix-1 (the DB migration) aligned the stored mapping with the sheet's actual header casing — so the router's exact-case row.get(col, '') succeeds. If a user renames a header again in future, the router's mapped_field will silently return '' for tracking_id / master_order_id / order_id, and dedupe by those keys will regress. Recommend porting the case-insensitive fallback + mapping_lc from server.py:1290-1370 into routers/sheets.py:273-292 for defence-in-depth.

rca_of_issue: Reported: /api/sheets/orders returned 329/329 as 'New Orders' after all 329 shipments were created. Root cause: settings.sheet.column_mapping stored uppercase 'Order ID' etc., but the actual sheet header is title-case 'Order Id'. The live handler in routers/sheets.py did an exact-case row.get(col, '') → returned '' for every field → sheet_order_id / sheet_tracking / sheet_master were all empty → the dedupe `if sheet_order_id and sheet_order_id in order_ids` short-circuited to False → every row was flagged not_shipped. Fix-1 (DB migration) rewrote every column_mapping value from 'X ID' → 'X Id' and injected the missing tracking_id/master_order_id entries — this ALONE resolves the live bug because now mapping matches sheet headers exactly. Fix-2 (server.py hardening) adds a case-insensitive fallback in the SERVER copy of the handler + _row_key, but only _row_key is actually reachable from the router; the server-side mapped_field lives on a dead code path. Verified end-to-end via GET /api/sheets/orders → 311/329 shipped correctly.
